In a quiet valley, a tortoise named Tiko gazed at the sky, watching birds soar above the treetops. Unlike his slow-moving kin, Tiko longed to rise above the earth, to feel the wind beneath his shell. One day, he stumbled upon a feathered wing from a fallen bird. With determination, he crafted wings from reeds and leaves, practicing daily until his limbs ached. Though his first attempts sent him tumbling into bushes, Tiko refused to quit.  

After months of trial and error, Tiko discovered that his heavy shell made flight impossible. Undeterred, he sought advice from a wise old owl, who suggested he lighten his load. Tiko shed his shell, but without it, he was vulnerable to predators. He tried again, this time carrying only a small, hollow shell. With a final push, he soared—briefly—before crashing into a river.  

The next morning, Tiko emerged from the water, his shell intact but his wings broken. He realized that true flight required more than wings; it demanded balance, strength, and the wisdom to know when to let go. Though he never flew again, Tiko learned to glide along the river’s surface, content with his own unique way of moving through the world.  

**Moral:** Sometimes, the journey teaches us more than the destination.
